Nvidia’s board announced on Sunday that it is launching an independent investigation.
This follows reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation.
The board stated that a committee of independent directors will oversee the review.
They are working with outside legal counsel to examine the situation.
The announcement came after a memo from Huang circulated among employees.
He admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Megaspeed.
The board said Huang fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it.
They expressed confidence in his leadership team despite the ongoing inquiry.
A memo circulating among U.S. policymakers earlier this year claimed Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security.
The goal was to spy on Nvidia’s CEO.
In his memo, Huang apologized to his family and colleagues for his actions.
He stated that he was unfaithful to his wife and hurt their children.
He acknowledged that he had fallen short of his responsibility to the company.
Nvidia previously said that interactions between the pair were not unusual.
The company also noted that it does not share classified information with customers.
The board emphasized that it prioritizes U.S. national and economic security above all else.
Chips, especially Nvidia’s, have been a major focus as the AI race between the United States and China heats up.
Other companies involved in the AI boom have warned employees to be wary of possible spies.
These warnings include threats from individuals offering sex or romance.
The board stated it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.
However, the inquiry will examine all available information to ensure safety.
This context highlights the strategic importance of Nvidia in the current geopolitical landscape.

Apple is working to make Siri more agentic, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman.
CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI leader Craig Federighi to speed up the roadmap.
The goal is to deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse.
The company acknowledges it is not keeping pace with rivals.
This push aims to close the gap in consumer AI capabilities.
Two key upgrades are expected soon.
First, Siri will gain fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps.
This allows actions like rotating images in Photos or organizing Safari tabs.
These features are expected in iOS 27.3.
Second, Siri will integrate with third-party apps.
This could let users place orders via Grubhub or book tables on OpenTable.
Gurman says this larger change is likely to land in the Spring.
Agentic AI means the system can perform ongoing tasks without user prompts.
It tracks goals and decides the next steps automatically.
Current assistants mostly handle one-off requests.
Apple wants Siri to pursue objectives independently.
This shift is driven by market demands and competitor features.
It changes how users interact with their devices daily.

They choose Google Health Coach and press the Turn off button.
